hints: Focus on what a mass spectrum really shows, the mass numbers of the separate isotopes and how abundant each one is.
Remember copper has two main isotopes at $m/e$ 63 and 65, so look for a chart with just those two peaks.
Use the weighted average idea, the $A_r$ of 63.5 is exactly halfway between 63 and 65, then check which peak ratio gives that average.
walkthrough:
**Recall what $A_r$ means**

Think of relative atomic mass as a weighted average of all the isotopes. Heavier isotopes pull the average up, lighter ones pull it down, depending on abundance.

$$A_r = \frac{\sum (\text{isotopic mass} \times \text{% abundance})}{100}$$

**Spot the sensible isotopes for copper**

Copper is known to have two isotopes, $^{63}\text{Cu}$ and $^{65}\text{Cu}$. So we expect just two peaks at $m/e$ 63 and 65. That already points strongly to one chart.

**Test the calculation for that chart**

For the chart with 74% at 63 and 26% at 65:

$$A_r = \frac{(63 \times 74) + (65 \times 26)}{100} = \frac{4662 + 1690}{100} = \frac{6352}{100} = 63.52$$

**Conclude with confidence**

63.52 rounds to 63.5, exactly the given value. The roughly 3:1 ratio makes sense because 63.5 is much closer to 63 than to 65, so the lighter isotope must dominate.

options.A: Shows a single peak at about $m/e$ 63.5 with 100% abundance. Isotopes always have whole number mass numbers, you cannot have a $^{63.5}\text{Cu}$ isotope. $A_r$ can be non-integer, but individual peaks cannot.
options.B: Shows three peaks at 62, 63 and 65. Copper does not have three isotopes in this pattern, and the weighted average is too high: $(62 \times 17 + 63 \times 33 + 65 \times 50)/100 = 63.83$, not 63.5.
options.C: Shows exactly the two copper isotopes, $^{63}\text{Cu}$ at 74% and $^{65}\text{Cu}$ at 26%. The weighted average is $(63 \times 74 + 65 \times 26)/100 = 63.52$, which rounds to 63.5. The larger 63 peak correctly pulls the average close to 63.
options.D: Shows four peaks at 61, 62, 65 and 66. Copper does not have this set of isotopes. Its weighted average is $(61 \times 33 + 62 \times 22 + 65 \times 12 + 66 \times 33)/100 = 63.35$, not 63.5.
